AggregationLevel: Per-Equipment (fleet/class views aggregate this per-equipment value by simple average)
NullBehavior: Null if <2 failures (not zero, not error)
ZeroDivisionBehavior: N/A - denominator is (count-1), guarded by the >=2 minimum so denominator is always >=1
DateFilterBehavior: None applied at MTBF calculation itself - Index/Intelligence pages apply from/to to Pareto/Trend queries, NOT to this per-equipment MTBF calculation (verified: GetEquipmentReliabilityAsync takes no date parameters)
FunctionalLocationFilterBehavior: Not applied (no FunctionalLocation filter in this query)
EquipmentClassFilterBehavior: Not applied at equipment level (class-level aggregation exists separately via GetClassReliabilityAsync)
FailureInclusionRule: All IsActive=true FailureRecords for the equipment regardless of any other field completeness
KnownLimitations: Calendar-time span, not operating-time; no exclusion of future-dated or duplicate-timestamp records; degenerate case of duplicate FailureDate at both ends yields MTBF=0 exactly (a valid float, not null) which can look like a real 'near-zero MTBF' result to a viewer
EngineeringMeaning: A time-between-events indicator over calendar time - not an industry-standard operating-time-normalized MTBF estimate
SafeToDocument: Yes - as a calendar-time indicator with the stated limitation

ImplementedFormula: Average of (WorkOrder.CompletionDate - WorkOrder.StartDate).TotalHours over failures whose linked WorkOrder has both dates set
RequiredMinimumData: >=1 FailureRecord with a linked WorkOrder that has both StartDate and CompletionDate populated
NullBehavior: Null if no qualifying failure/WorkOrder pair exists
ZeroDivisionBehavior: N/A (simple average; no division risk from the average itself)
FailureInclusionRule: Only FailureRecords with WorkOrderId set AND that WorkOrder having both StartDate and CompletionDate
WorkOrderDependency: Direct - requires a linked, dated WorkOrder; unlinked FailureRecords silently excluded from MTTR (they still count toward MTBF and FailureCount)
DowntimeTreatment: Not used in MTTR (downtime hours and repair-duration hours are two separate concepts in this implementation - DowntimeHours feeds TotalDowntimeHours/Pareto/Bad-Actor
EngineeringMeaning: CONFIRMED GAP (G-1): no guard against CompletionDate < StartDate (negative duration) - PEMS's own ReliabilityDataQualityService already counts this exact condition (FailureRecordsWithNegativeDuration) as a data-quality issue, but ReliabilityService's MTTR average does not exclude or clamp it. Also includes any non-repair elapsed time (waiting/logistics/permit) that occurred inside the WorkOrder's Start-to-Completion window - not pure hands-on repair time.
SafeToDocument: Elapsed Work-Order duration, not isolated repair/wrench time
VerificationStatus: Yes - as elapsed-duration MTTR with the stated limitations

ImplementedFormula: MTBFHours / (MTBFHours + MTTRHours) * 100 - only when both have a value and their sum > 0
AggregationLevel: Per-Equipment (class level = simple average of equipment-level Availability values - see GetClassReliabilityAsync)
RequiredMinimumData: Both MTBF and MTTR must be non-null (so implicitly >=2 failures AND >=1 completed linked WorkOrder)
NullBehavior: Null if either MTBF or MTTR is null
ZeroDivisionBehavior: Explicit guard: (MTBFHours + MTTRHours) > 0 required, so exact 0/0 cannot occur; result stays null instead
DateFilterBehavior: Inherits MTBF/MTTR's lack of date filtering at this layer
EquipmentClassFilterBehavior: Class-level value is an AVERAGE OF PERCENTAGES, not a recomputation from aggregated class MTBF/MTTR - CONFIRMED via code read of GetClassReliabilityAsync (availabilityValues.Average())
KnownLimitations: CONFIRMED GAP (G-1 continued): mathematically NOT bounded to 0-100% - a negative MTTR (from a negative-duration WorkOrder) can push the ratio above 100% or into other unintuitive ranges, since the formula only guards against a zero denominator, not against the sign or magnitude of MTTR. Class-level average-of-percentages can be skewed by low-sample-size equipment carrying equal weight to high-sample-size equipment.
EngineeringMeaning: The standard textbook Inherent Availability formula, applied to the above (non-industry-standard) MTBF/MTTR inputs
SafeToDocument: Yes - with an explicit 'not bounded to 0-100%' caveat added this increment

SourceFields: FailureRecord.FailureDate (for date range);FailureRecord.DowntimeHours;FailureRecord.FailureMode/FailureCause (string fields - NOT the FK reference fields)
ImplementedFormula: Top-N (default 20, or 10 from Dashboard) equipment with >0 failures in the date range, ordered by FailureCount descending then TotalDowntimeHours descending
NullBehavior: Equipment with 0 failures in range is excluded entirely (not shown with a zero rank)
EquipmentFilterBehavior: Applied to the FailureHistory events within each equipment (not to equipment inclusion itself - an equipment with failures outside the range but none inside is excluded)
FunctionalLocationFilterBehavior: Implicit only via the fleet source list (no direct equipment-id filter parameter)
FailureInclusionRule: Not applied (EquipmentClassName is displayed but not filterable in this method)
WorkOrderDependency: Uses the same fleet source (FailureRecords.IsActive) as MTBF/MTTR - inherits their inclusion rule
DowntimeTreatment: Indirect - MTBFHours/MTTRHours shown per Bad Actor are pulled from the already-computed EquipmentReliabilityDto (no parallel calculation)
KnownLimitations: Used as the tie-break sort key after FailureCount
EngineeringMeaning: No configurable threshold exists - it is always top-N, never 'any equipment exceeding X'. RepeatFailureCount uses a fixed, non-configurable 90-day window. Deterministic tie-breaking is only 2 levels deep (FailureCount, then DowntimeHours) - true 3-way ties fall back to input-list stable-sort order, not an explicit key like EquipmentId. Correctly uses the free-text FailureMode/FailureCause fields (NOT affected by the FailureModeId/FailureCauseId gap that affects the Pareto charts).
SafeToDocument: A descriptive worst-N ranking by failure frequency (then downtime) - not a prescriptive/weighted risk score, not a formally standard-defined 'Bad Actor' methodology
VerificationStatus: Yes - as a descriptive top-N ranking with the stated tie-break/threshold limitations

SourceFields: FailureRecord.FailureModeRef (FK navigation - NOT the FailureMode string field)
ImplementedFormula: GROUP BY FailureModeRef.Name / FailureCauseRef.Name, filtered to FailureModeRef != null / FailureCauseRef != null, with cumulative percent
NullBehavior: Empty list if no records qualify (not an error)
FailureInclusionRule: Only records with the FK reference populated
KnownLimitations: CONFIRMED CRITICAL GAP (G-2): FailureRecord.FailureModeId/FailureCauseId are NEVER set by any code path in the entire codebase (verified by exhaustive grep) - the only write path to FailureRecord (WorkOrderLifecycleService.SyncFailureRecordAsync) only sets the free-text FailureMode/FailureCause strings, not the FK fields. This means these two Pareto charts will return an EMPTY result regardless of how much real failure data exists, until either the sync logic is extended to resolve/set the FK or these queries are changed to group by the string fields instead.
EngineeringMeaning: Intended as a taxonomy-driven Pareto (80/20) analysis of failure modes/causes
SafeToDocument: No - do not document this as a working feature without the fix; if documented at all it must state it is currently non-functional
SMEReviewRequired: Yes - product decision needed on which side (sync logic or query) to fix

ImplementedFormula: (TotalFailureRecords - FailureRecordsWithoutFailureMode) / TotalFailureRecords * 100, where FailureRecordsWithoutFailureMode counts FailureModeId==null
KnownLimitations: Same root cause as G-2 - since FailureModeId is never set anywhere, this metric is structurally guaranteed to read ~0% regardless of actual data quality, making it a misleading 'always red' indicator as currently wired rather than a genuine quality signal
SafeToDocument: pre-existing data-quality diagnostic - not built this increment
VerificationStatus: No - flag as structurally miscalibrated until G-2 is addressed
